items.title: Hilton Says It Will Build New Brands Again — Owners Will Want to See the Math
items.summary: A trademark and a domain suggest that a new Hilton lifestyle brand called Tortoise may be in the works. But the bigger question for the newish chief development officer is whether Hilton's model still mints the best returns for owners.

items.title: World Cup Week 1: Boosting Hotel Revenue, But Occupancy Lags
items.summary: The global soccer tournament is juicing revenue per available room, even if it’s not delivering the occupancies hotels had been expecting.

items.title: Karak Chai, Luxury Retail, and the Invisible Millions of the Gulf Hub Airports: An Audio Essay
items.summary: The largest purpose-driven travel flow on earth passes through the most commercially aspirational spaces on earth, and the dissonance is jarring if you stop long enough to watch who is actually walking past the glittering Hermes store...

items.title: Air New Zealand’s Tech-Savvy CEO on AI and the Limits of the Machine
items.summary: An AI-powered airline is a fine ambition – but it won't touch the fuel price, the grounded engines, or the weak Kiwi dollar doing the real damage. Ravishankar's edge is that he seems to know it.

items.title: Grab Says Its Travel Strategy Isn’t About Hotels or Flights, It’s About Knowing What You’ll Need Next
items.summary: Grab says it isn't competing with the region’s travel platforms. But what it is building may be more disruptive than direct competition.

items.title: Airbnb Moves Into Fintech With a Cancel-for-Any-Reason Feature
items.summary: Airbnb is selling peace of mind to guests, giving assurances to hosts, and potentially debuting a new fintech revenue stream that’s been so successful for Hopper. The issue is whether this will further alienate hosts, who deal with the logistical hassles of last-minute cancellati

items.title: The Best Luxury Experiences Leave Some Slack in the System
items.summary: The marketing from luxury's top brands has blurred into one seamless, forgettable product. The operators pulling away are the ones who figured out that friction is the point.

items.title: UK and Australia Lift Gulf Travel Warnings, But European Airlines Await Clearance
items.summary: Gulf travel advisories are moving. War-risk insurance authorization isn’t — and that’s the constraint that controls when European airlines come back.
